results.problem: Multiple Source Shortest Paths (MSSP) on undirected unweighted graphs
results.quote: MSSP on undirected unweighted graphs is equivalent to BMM(|S_in|,n,n), up to n^{o(1)} factors, for randomized algorithms. In particular, there is a randomized algorithm computing MSSP on undirected, unweighted graphs in n^{o(1)}T_{BMM}(|S_in|,n,n) time.

results.problem: Multiple Source Shortest Paths (MSSP) on undirected graphs with integer edge weights in [B]
results.quote: MSSP on undirected graphs with integer edge weights in [B] is equivalent to MPP(|S_in|,n,n|B), up to n^{o(1)} log B factors, for randomized algorithms. In particular, if B \le \mathrm{poly}(n), there is a randomized algorithm computing MSSP on undirected graphs with integer edge weights in [B] in n^{o(1)}T_{MPP}(|S_in|,n,n|B) time.

results.bound: n^{2+o(1)} \text{ time algorithm that computes a } (2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}, 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})})\text{-LDSND}
results.quote: There is a randomized n^{2+o(1)} time algorithm that computes a (2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}, 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})})-low diameter small neighborhood decomposition.

results.problem: \beta-hop-set construction on undirected graphs with integer weights
results.bound: B n^{o(1)} \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MUL}}(n/\beta,n,n) \text{ time algorithm that computes a } \beta\text{-hop-set with } \widetilde{O}(n^2/\beta^2) \text{ edges}
results.quote: For all \beta \ge 1, there is a randomized B n^{o(1)} T_{MUL}(n/\beta,n,n) time algorithm that computes a \beta-hop-set with \widetilde{O}(n^2/\beta^2) edges on undirected graphs with integer weights in [B].

results.problem: +4-emulator construction on undirected graphs with integer weights
results.bound: O(B n^{\omega(1,2/3,1)+o(1)}) = O(B n^{2.1321}) \text{ time algorithm to construct } +4B\text{-emulators of size } O(n^{4/3}\log n)
results.quote: There is a randomized O(B n^{\omega(1,2/3,1)+o(1)}) = O(B n^{2.1321}) time algorithm to construct +4B-emulators of size O(n^{4/3} log n) on undirected graphs with integer weights at most B.

results.problem: Multiple Source Reachability in directed graphs
results.quote: Multiple Source Reachability is equivalent to BMM(|S_in|,n,n), up to polylog(n) factors. In particular, there is a deterministic algorithm computing Multiple-Source Reachability in \widetilde{O}(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(|S_\mathrm{in}|,n,n)) time.

results.problem: MSSP on unweighted directed acyclic graphs
results.previous_best: \widetilde{O}(\max_{1\le t\le n} \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(s+t, t, n | n/t)) \text{ (Grandoni and Vassilevska Williams)}
results.quote: There is a deterministic algorithm computing MSSP on unweighted directed acyclic graphs in \widetilde{O}(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(|S_\mathrm{in}|,n,n|n,1)) time.

results.problem: Shortcut set computation in directed graphs
results.bound: \widetilde{O}(n^2 + \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n/D^2, n, n | D, 1)) \text{ time for } D=O(\sqrt{n})
results.quote: For D=O(\sqrt{n}), there is an algorithm that computes a D-shortcut-set of size \widetilde{O}(n^2/D^3+n) in time \widetilde{O}(n^2+\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n/D^2,n,n|D,1)).

results.problem: Min-Plus Product with Distinct Entry Bounds
results.bound: \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n_1,n_2,n_3|B_1,B_2) = O(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1 B_1, n_2, n_3 B_2)) \text{ and if } B=B_1+B_2, \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n_1,n_2,n_3|B_1,B_2) = O(\min(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1 B, n_2 B_2, n_3), \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1, n_2 B_1, n_3 B)))
results.quote: Suppose \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(a,b,c)=\Omega(ab+ac+bc). For any integers n_1,n_2,n_3,B_1,B_2,B \ge 0, \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n_1,n_2,n_3|B_1,B_2)=O(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1 B_1,n_2,n_3 B_2)) and if B=B_1+B_2, \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{MPP}}(n_1,n_2,n_3|B_1,B_2)=O(\min(\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1 B,n_2 B_2,n_3), \mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{BMM}}(n_1,n_2 B_1,n_3 B))).
